entries.title: Ruth 2:2
segments:
Glean ears; pick up what was scattered and left in the field by the reapers. 
 
  Grace; favor. 
 
True piety will lead those who have it to be industrious, and to engage in any honest, useful employment to which they may in the providence of God be called.

entries.title: Ruth 2:3
segments:
A part of the field; the cultivated fields were not then ordinarily divided by fences, but by a stone or landmark. 
 
With a fatherly kindness God watches over and directs the concerns of the poorest, most obscure, and defenceless of his people, and directs them in such a manner as to promote their highest good.

entries.title: Ruth 2:4
segments: Love to God inspires goodwill to men, and promotes kind affection and true politeness in all conditions and relations of life.

entries.title: Ruth 2:7
segments: In the house; probably the tent pitched in the field where the reapers were at work, and under which Boaz saw her sitting; for she does not seem to have gone home to her mother in Bethlehem until evening.

entries.title: Ruth 2:8
segments:
Hearest thou not; hearken. 
 
  My daughter; an expression of kindness. 
 
Kindness to the destitute, especially to the stranger, the widow, the fatherless, and those who have no earthly helper, is peculiarly pleasing to God and endearing to men.

entries.title: Ruth 2:10
segments: She fell on her face; a common mode in those regions of expressing reverence and gratitude.

entries.title: Ruth 2:11
segments: Affectionate regard to parents and other relatives, and sacrifices for their benefit from love to God and his cause, are always remembered by him, and often even in this life receive a great reward.

entries.title: Ruth 2:13
segments:
Like unto one of thy handmaidens; as a foreigner she did not venture to put herself in the same rank with them. 
 
The humble, who esteem others better than themselves, are often exalted by God's providence above the proud and self-conceited.  Thus the modest Ruth became the wife of a "mighty man of wealth," and the ancestor of David and of Him who is greater than David.  All this earthly favor was but the earnest and pledge of that heavenly exaltation which is reserved for the meek and lowly in spirit.

entries.title: Ruth 2:14
segments: Vinegar; a kind of sour wine or sauce used in those days.

entries.title: Ruth 2:15
segments: A generous mind will avoid reproaches and every thing calculated to wound the feelings of the poor, and will delight to aid them in their efforts, by industry and economy, to provide for themselves and those dependent upon them.

entries.title: Ruth 2:19
segments: In answer to the prayers of the pious poor for blessings on those who supply their wants, the rich often receive treasures better and more abundant than all which they bestow.

entries.title: Ruth 2:20
segments: One of our next kinsmen; one who according to the law had a right to redeem.

entries.title: Ruth 2:22
segments: When in a course which we find by experience to be safe and useful, and in which the Lord blesses us, it is ordinarily wise to persevere and not be disposed to change.  This the aged and experienced feel more deeply than the inexperienced and young.
